basic_info.title: Mastering Atari with Discrete World Models (DreamerV2)
basic_info.affiliation: Google Research / University of Toronto (Hafner; consortium not fully confirmed from abstract page)
basic_info.code_available: danijar.com/dreamerv2 (website referenced; repo not confirmed from abstract page)

method.notes: Introduces the RSSM with CATEGORICAL (not Gaussian) stochastic latents and straight-through gradients, trained purely from imagined latent rollouts, achieving human-level performance on 55 Atari games. Introduces KL BALANCING: instead of a single symmetric KL term, the loss is split into a 'dynamics loss' (prior trained to match a stop-gradiented posterior) and a 'representation loss' (posterior trained to match a stop-gradiented prior), weighted asymmetrically (dynamics weighted higher than representation in V2's ablations) so the prior is pushed to track the posterior more strongly than the reverse -- this deliberately makes it cheap for the posterior to carry information and expensive for the prior to stay ignorant, directly relevant to why a purely SYMMETRIC free-bits floor (as used in Stage-2 Runs 1/2') can leave collapse unaddressed. Also introduces the KL free-bits floor (clip below ~1 nat, no gradient) used verbatim in Stage-2's Change 1/11.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Model-based RL for Atari pixel control, not GPS map matching. Confirms P2 (latent-world-model RL) architecture exists and is the source of the RSSM formula reused in Stage 2, but never touches road graphs, GPS, or map matching.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: Same class as Think2Drive -- architectural inspiration for P2, wrong domain entirely; does not pre-empt the thesis's GPS map-matching application.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Primary architectural source for Stage 2's RSSM (GRU + categorical latents, KL balancing, free bits) and the direct precedent for diagnosing why Stage 2's SYMMETRIC KL treatment (Runs 1/2') failed to prevent posterior collapse -- V2's asymmetric dynamics/representation split was not yet tried in this project.

uncertain: Exact numeric KL-balance weights used in DreamerV2 specifically (vs. DreamerV3's 0.5/0.1) were not confirmed from the abstract page; DreamerV3's paper (see dreamerv3_diverse_domains.json) is the more precise numeric source already used in this project's Change 1.
